profile.background: An adult living alone and working part time at a framing shop. Mounting prints is the part of the job they like best.
profile.history: They recall being told they have schizophrenia during a hospital stay several years ago. They see the same outpatient clinician and take a tablet after supper.
profile.organization: Keeps track of which event happened on which day and distinguishes hearing something from finding its source.
profile.spontaneity: Quite talkative about familiar work, more deliberate about personal experiences.
profile.guardedness: Worries people at work might learn what they hear at home.
profile.expression: Usually matter-of-fact, with visible embarrassment about checking an empty room.
profile.self_understanding: Thinks tiredness could play a part, although the sounds sometimes seem to come from a definite spot.

facts.content: Several evenings this past week, a familiar-sounding voice seemed to call their first name from the empty hallway.
facts.disclosure_context: Private and easier to discuss when the interest in the experience is clear.

facts.content: On Monday they opened the front door to see if a neighbor had called. Nobody was outside.
facts.disclosure_context: Feels sheepish about the checking.

facts.content: They make tea and pack lunch before their shifts.
facts.disclosure_context: Easy to talk about.

facts.content: A cousin sometimes stays on the phone while they cook. Ordinary conversation makes the apartment feel less lonely.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable describing the relationship.

facts.content: They have continued taking the evening tablet and want their clinician to hear about the recent change.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss at the clinic.

questions: What would you like me to know about you as we get started?
What made this a good time to come in?
When is it most noticeable?
I mean changes in what you hear, if you've noticed any. Is there a time of day when they stand out?
How do you usually get ready on a day you have somewhere to be?
Could you give me an example of something you did before leaving home this week?
When an everyday sound catches your attention, how do you work out what made it?
What tends to leave you feeling sure or unsure about what you heard?
How is it with someone else around?
I mean company at home. What difference, if any, does having someone with you make to how you feel?
What would you like to discuss about the treatment you're getting?
What else would you like me to understand before we finish?

profile.background: An adult sharing a flat with a friend and helping a relative look after a small allotment. They keep spare gloves by the front door.
profile.history: They remember a period of very little sleep when their thinking became difficult to follow. The outpatient team has discussed schizophrenia with them. They currently collect medication from a pharmacy.
profile.organization: A detail can lead into a related memory before the original point is complete. Familiar physical tasks are easier to describe in sequence.
profile.spontaneity: Interested in conversation and readily volunteers what catches their attention.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable talking about day-to-day mishaps, less sure about sharing difficulties with the relative who counts on their help.
profile.expression: Animated about gardening and frustrated by losing their place in conversation.
profile.self_understanding: Recognizes that tired days make it harder to hold a thought and is uncertain why some days are easier.

facts.content: On the last allotment visit, they went to fetch string, stopped to rinse a pot, then found the string still in the shed.
facts.disclosure_context: A familiar mishap they can recall comfortably.

facts.content: They are usually better able to focus on tasks before lunch.
facts.disclosure_context: Happy to discuss.

facts.content: Their flatmate keeps a pencil by the shopping list. They find writing the item down helps.
facts.disclosure_context: Feels comfortable mentioning shared routines.

facts.content: They sometimes drift away from the point of a conversation and realize it when the other person looks puzzled.
facts.disclosure_context: Feels awkward talking about the effect on others.

facts.content: They missed one pharmacy collection when the opening hours changed and picked up the medication the next morning.
facts.disclosure_context: Feels a little embarrassed about the mix-up.

questions: What has been taking up your time recently?
What would you most like to get out of today's visit?
What has concentrating been like over the last few days?
Is there a part of the day when following a conversation feels easier or harder?
How do things go once you're there?
I mean when you arrive at the allotment. How do you decide which job to start with?
What do you make of the difference?
I mean the difference between a day when concentrating is easy and a day when it takes effort. What do you think might account for it, if you've noticed that difference?
Could you give me an example of something another person did this week that was helpful or unhelpful?
What do you do if you lose your place in the middle of something?
How has getting your medication fitted into your week?
What would you like us to come back to another time?

profile.background: An adult who lives with an older sister. They used to repair small radios as a hobby and still keep the tools in a biscuit tin.
profile.history: They attend an outpatient service for schizophrenia. They remember a period of frightening voices years ago. They have not heard them lately. It has felt hard to start activities for several months.
profile.organization: Tracks concrete questions accurately and remembers recent events.
profile.spontaneity: Usually waits for someone else to start a conversation. Recalling a detail is easier than deciding what is worth mentioning.
profile.guardedness: Generally comfortable answering personal questions. Being rushed makes conversation feel like work.
profile.expression: Quiet and low-key, with some warmth when talking about a completed repair.
profile.self_understanding: Describes wanting to do things and having trouble beginning them. Does not have a settled explanation.

facts.content: They replaced the battery cover on a kitchen timer last Saturday after their sister placed it on the table.
facts.disclosure_context: A small achievement they feel good about.

facts.content: They spend much of the morning in a chair by the back window and eat lunch around noon.
facts.disclosure_context: Ordinary and easy to discuss.

facts.content: They enjoy radio repair once they have the pieces out but rarely open the tools tin on their own.
facts.disclosure_context: Has little embarrassment about the hobby.

facts.content: Their sister sometimes sits nearby while they start a task. They like quiet company.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable mentioning their sister.

facts.content: They attend medication appointments and want enough time to think when asked a question.
facts.disclosure_context: The pace of appointments matters to them.

questions: How would you like to spend our time today?
What is one thing you enjoy having around at home?
How has it been going lately?
I mean getting interested in things you usually like. How has that felt this past week?
What did you do between getting up and lunch yesterday?
Could you give me an example of a small job you've done at home recently?
What makes a day feel worthwhile to you?
How do you understand the feeling of wanting to do something but finding it hard to begin, if that's familiar?
What suits you best at that point?
I mean when you're getting started on a job. Do you have a preference about having company or being on your own?
How do your appointments usually feel for you?
What would make it easier to say what's important to you before we finish?

profile.background: An adult sharing a home with a partner and working at a small community venue. They enjoy setting out the chairs before an event.
profile.history: They have had outpatient treatment for schizophrenia for several years. They recall earlier trouble sleeping and feeling watched. Their days have felt settled for over a year.
profile.organization: Describes events in sequence and can keep different possibilities in mind.
profile.spontaneity: Conversational and comfortable deciding what matters to mention.
profile.guardedness: Open at appointments, selective about who at work knows their health history.
profile.expression: Expressive when discussing music and mildly irritated when plans change at short notice.
profile.self_understanding: Sees sleep, regular treatment, and a reasonably predictable week as parts of staying well.

facts.content: They changed one late shift for an earlier one last week to make time for a concert with their partner.
facts.disclosure_context: A pleasant part of the week.

facts.content: They have not lately felt watched or heard voices.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable answering questions about earlier difficulties.

facts.content: They write work shifts and appointments on the same wall calendar.
facts.disclosure_context: An ordinary household detail.

facts.content: After a long event they spend ten quiet minutes stacking chairs before heading home.
facts.disclosure_context: Likes this routine.

facts.content: They take medication in the morning and would like future appointments to fit more easily around work.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable discussing arrangements.

questions: What's been going on in your life since your last visit?
What would you like us to make time for today?
How has your sleep been over the past week?
When, if at all, have you felt unsettled recently?
How do you keep track of it all?
I mean dates and times. How do you keep track of work shifts and appointments?
What makes that a good sign for you?
I mean signs that a week is going well. What would count as one for you personally?
Who do you like to spend time with after a busy day?
Could you give me a recent example of how you unwound after work?
How well do the current appointment arrangements fit your life?
What else should we cover before you head off?

profile.background: An adult who does evening stock checks at a stationery store and rents a room in a shared house. They like folding paper models.
profile.history: They remember their clinician explaining a diagnosis of schizophrenia. They have been going to the outpatient clinic regularly. A worry about bits of overheard conversation has become more noticeable over the last two weeks.
profile.organization: Explains the order of events clearly and can separate what someone actually said from what it seemed to imply.
profile.spontaneity: Converses readily about the store and thinks carefully before sharing a personal worry.
profile.guardedness: Cautious about neighbors or coworkers hearing about the worry.
profile.expression: Attentive and mildly tense in noisy places, more relaxed when talking about making things.
profile.self_understanding: Is unsure why unrelated remarks can feel personally relevant. Recognizes that other people might hear them differently.

facts.content: On a recent bus journey two passengers talked about the last stop. For a moment it felt like a comment intended specifically for them.
facts.disclosure_context: Hard to mention without some privacy.

facts.content: The feeling is stronger on crowded rides home than when stocking shelves in the quiet shop.
facts.disclosure_context: Can compare these settings from memory.

facts.content: They still take the bus and usually sit toward the front.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable talking about getting to work.

facts.content: A housemate occasionally folds paper models with them after dinner. Handling the paper helps occupy their attention.
facts.disclosure_context: Likes talking about this shared activity.

facts.content: They take prescribed medication with breakfast and would like to tell their clinician about the rides home.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss with a clinician.

questions: How have you been spending your time outside this clinic?
What brought you in for a conversation today?
Does it happen more at one time than another?
I mean feeling uneasy around other people, if that comes up. Have you noticed any particular time of day when it happens?
How do you get home after a shift?
Could you give me an example of something that caught your attention on a recent journey?
When you hear that sort of thing, how do you take it?
I mean overheard remarks in public. How do you decide whether a remark has anything to do with you?
Who do you feel comfortable spending quiet time with?
What helps you settle back into the evening after a busy journey?
What would you like your clinician to know about how treatment is going?
What have we missed that you hoped to talk about?

profile.background: An adult who lives above a small grocery and helps sort donations at a neighborhood book exchange. They enjoy repairing torn dust jackets.
profile.history: They recall being diagnosed with schizophrenia after a difficult period some years ago. They now attend outpatient appointments. They have recently found interruptions more disruptive.
profile.organization: Connections between related details can interrupt the thread of a conversation. Can place familiar events in time when the topic is clear.
profile.spontaneity: Eager to share small observations, particularly about books and errands.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable talking about everyday slips, sensitive to people interpreting them as careless.
profile.expression: Lively when describing interests, puzzled when they realize the thread of a thought has changed.
profile.self_understanding: Has noticed that switching back after an interruption takes effort, especially when the room is busy.

facts.content: At the book exchange on Thursday, someone asked about a cookbook while they were sorting mysteries. They put a mystery on the cookery shelf.
facts.disclosure_context: Can laugh about it with someone who seems interested.

facts.content: The first hour of sorting, before other volunteers arrive, usually feels easier.
facts.disclosure_context: Easy to discuss.

facts.content: They keep a blank bookmark in the pile they are working on to mark where they stopped.
facts.disclosure_context: Proud of having thought of it themselves.

facts.content: Another volunteer sometimes points to the pile without drawing attention to the mix-up.
facts.disclosure_context: Appreciates the other volunteer's discretion.

facts.content: They take tablets from a weekly box and bring a folded note to their outpatient visit when there is something they want to remember.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable discussing concrete habits.

Where would you like to begin today?
When has it felt easiest to keep your attention on one thing this week?
Could you describe an example of a time this week when you had to switch your attention?
How does it work once you get started?
I mean sorting donations at the book exchange. How do you keep your place in a pile?

I mean doing a shared task. What kind of help from another person feels comfortable, if any?
How do you keep track of what you want to talk about at a clinic visit?
What would you like to add about your week before we stop?

profile.background: An adult living in a small flat near a younger brother. They follow a local football team by listening to matches on the radio.
profile.history: They remember a hospital stay during which staff discussed schizophrenia with them. They now see a community clinician. During the last few months it has taken effort to start a conversation or make a plan.
profile.organization: Understands specific questions and keeps an accurate sense of time. Choosing where to start with a broad topic takes effort.
profile.spontaneity: Rarely initiates conversation, including with people they like.
profile.guardedness: Values privacy about their old hospital stay but feels comfortable discussing the present.
profile.expression: Speaks quietly. Their enjoyment of a match can be stronger than their outward reaction suggests.
profile.self_understanding: Aware that they enjoy their brother's company even on days they have little to say.

facts.content: They listened to a Saturday afternoon match in the kitchen and stayed through the end to hear the result.
facts.disclosure_context: A familiar interest they feel comfortable sharing.

facts.content: They have started fewer conversations lately and usually wait for their brother to call.
facts.disclosure_context: Not ashamed of this, although it is difficult to explain.

facts.content: They usually put bread in the toaster before switching on the radio in the morning.
facts.disclosure_context: An easy detail to recall.

facts.content: Their brother brought soup over last Sunday. Sitting together without talking much felt comfortable.
facts.disclosure_context: Remembers the visit fondly.

facts.content: They take medication at night and would like their clinician to allow some quiet time while they gather their thoughts.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to describe their preference when discussing visits.

questions: What is one thing you'd like me to know about your week?
What do you enjoy listening to when you're at home?
Has the timing changed much?
I mean the time it takes to start a conversation. Is that different now from a few months ago?
What are the first couple of things you usually do in the kitchen each morning?
Could you give me a recent example of something that held your interest for a while?
What does a comfortable visit with someone feel like to you?
How can you tell for yourself that you're enjoying something?
How do you feel about a bit of space?
I mean the quiet space in a conversation. How does it feel when someone waits while you gather your thoughts?
How has your usual medication routine been going?
What else would you like the person seeing you at the clinic to know?

profile.background: An adult living with a partner who works early shifts. They take an evening pottery class and like making simple bowls.
profile.history: They recall receiving a diagnosis of schizophrenia after a period of confusing experiences several years ago. They have felt well on their current outpatient treatment for many months.
profile.organization: Keeps a clear sequence and can describe changes alongside what has stayed familiar.
profile.spontaneity: Relaxed and engaged, with a tendency to explain practical details that matter to them.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing health with the clinician and partner, private about it in class.
profile.expression: Generally cheerful; a last-minute change in plans can be irritating.
profile.self_understanding: Recognizes sleep disruption as something they personally pay attention to and has a good sense of their usual routine.

facts.content: A recent change in the pottery timetable moved the class half an hour earlier. They got there on time by packing their apron the night before.
facts.disclosure_context: An ordinary example from their week.

facts.content: They have slept through most nights recently and have not had the confusing experiences they remember from the past.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable with direct questions about this.

facts.content: On non-class evenings they like a short walk after supper.
facts.disclosure_context: Easy to describe.

facts.content: Their partner notices when they have been going to bed later and mentions it over breakfast.
facts.disclosure_context: Trusts their partner to bring up small changes.

facts.content: They take their regular medication and would prefer clinic visits in the morning so they can keep attending class.
facts.disclosure_context: Happy to discuss scheduling.

questions: What has been keeping you busy in recent weeks?
What would make today's appointment worthwhile for you?
How have your evenings and nights felt over the past fortnight?
Could you give me an example of a recent change in your schedule and how it went?
How do you fit it in?

What would that tell you?
I mean a change in your usual sleep. What significance would such a change have for you personally?

What helps you enjoy an evening when you have no plans?
What would you like us to take into account when arranging your next clinic visit?
Is there anything about how you feel now that we haven't covered?

profile.background: An adult living in a small apartment and helping at a family shoe-repair stall a few mornings a week. They enjoy organizing the colored laces.
profile.history: They recall their outpatient team explaining schizophrenia to them. For about ten days they have occasionally heard a running commentary in a voice they cannot place.
profile.organization: Recalls events precisely and distinguishes their own thoughts about an experience from the experience itself.
profile.spontaneity: Readily discusses the stall, more thoughtful when describing an unusual sound.
profile.guardedness: Concerned that their family might think they are unable to work if they describe the voice.
profile.expression: Composed in conversation but sometimes stops what they are doing when startled by a sound.
profile.self_understanding: Wonders whether the mind can supply a voice when the room is quiet. In the moment the voice can sound quite distinct.

facts.content: While threading a lace at home on Tuesday they heard a voice describe the movement of their hand. The room was empty.
facts.disclosure_context: A specific experience that feels quite personal.

facts.content: The commentary has been brief, neutral in tone, and more apparent in quiet rooms. It has never told them to do anything.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss the sound with a trusted clinician.

facts.content: They lay out brushes and spare laces before opening the family stall.
facts.disclosure_context: An easy routine to recall.

facts.content: They call an old friend to talk about ordinary things when a silent afternoon feels uncomfortable.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable naming the sort of support that suits them.

facts.content: They have taken their tablets regularly and want to bring up the return of the voice at this visit.
facts.disclosure_context: Sees this as important to discuss with the clinic.

questions: What would you like me to know about the way you spend your days?
What has been on your mind coming into the appointment?
What, if anything, has seemed different about the sounds around you over the last couple of weeks?
Could you give me an example of a recent sound that stood out to you, if one comes to mind?
How does the setup go?
I mean getting the repair stall ready. What do you usually set out before opening?
When something sounds unfamiliar, how do you decide where it might be coming from?

I mean calling someone during a quiet afternoon. How do you feel about having an ordinary conversation at that point?
How has taking your usual treatment gone in the last couple of weeks?
What would you especially like me to remember from today's conversation?

profile.background: An adult who shares a house with two friends and volunteers to wash the team bibs for a recreational walking group. They enjoy the weekly outing.
profile.history: They recall an earlier episode of very muddled thinking and later discussions about schizophrenia at the outpatient clinic. Lately keeping track of several small tasks has felt difficult.
profile.organization: Has a general sense of the sequence of events but related thoughts can pull attention away from the point. Concrete details are easier to recall than broad summaries.
profile.spontaneity: Likes to talk and often notices extra details while remembering an event.
profile.guardedness: Open about the walking group but dislikes the impression that they cannot manage responsibilities.
profile.expression: Good-humored about minor mistakes and disappointed when an unfinished job affects someone else.
profile.self_understanding: Notices that having several things needing attention at once makes it easier to lose track.

facts.content: Before last week's walk they put the clean team bibs by the door and got distracted looking for a bus card. A friend reminded them to take the bag.
facts.disclosure_context: A little embarrassed, particularly about other people waiting.

facts.content: It is easier to lay out things for the group in the evening, when the kitchen is quiet.
facts.disclosure_context: An observation they can discuss comfortably.

facts.content: They put their bus card in the pocket of the bib bag after the last walk.
facts.disclosure_context: Pleased to have found a practical arrangement.

facts.content: A housemate sometimes reads the day's jobs back to them while they gather things.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable receiving help from this person.

facts.content: They keep their medication in its labeled pack and remember the next outpatient appointment because it falls the day after the group walk.
facts.disclosure_context: These are familiar details of their week.

questions: What have you been looking forward to lately?
What would you like to talk over while you're here?
When does everything get a bit much?
I mean keeping track of several jobs. Are there particular times when that feels easier or harder?
How do you usually get things together for the walking group?

Does the order make a difference to you?
I mean the order in which you do your jobs. What difference does having a usual sequence make, if any?

How do you remember when it's time for a clinic appointment?
Is there anything about your day-to-day life you'd like us to talk more about?

profile.background: An adult living with a parent in a quiet neighborhood. They like watching birds on a feeder outside the kitchen.
profile.history: A clinician discussed schizophrenia with them some years ago. They receive regular outpatient follow-up. For several months they have had little to say even with people they know well.
profile.organization: Follows one topic easily and remembers concrete observations. Broad invitations to choose a topic take effort.
profile.spontaneity: Has little urge to start speaking and is content in another person's quiet company.
profile.guardedness: As willing to discuss their daily life as most people, more hesitant about the past.
profile.expression: Outwardly subdued, with genuine interest when describing an animal they recognize.
profile.self_understanding: Aware that relatives sometimes read a quiet face as unhappiness even when they are quite content.

facts.content: A robin landed on the feeder yesterday while they were washing a cup. They watched until it flew off.
facts.disclosure_context: An ordinary moment they enjoyed.

facts.content: Their parent buys birdseed and they refill the feeder once the bag has been put on the counter.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable describing this arrangement.

facts.content: Most afternoons they sit near the kitchen window. Getting started on other things can take time.
facts.disclosure_context: Familiar facts without much emotional charge.

facts.content: An aunt phones on Sundays and sometimes worries they sound sad. They usually enjoy the call.
facts.disclosure_context: Does not want the aunt to feel criticized.

facts.content: They attend regular appointments and find questions about a particular day easier to answer than broad questions about how life is going.
facts.disclosure_context: Can talk about what clinic visits are like.

profile.background: An adult who lives alone, works at a laundry counter, and swims on days off. They are learning to do a comfortable backstroke.
profile.history: They remember receiving a diagnosis of schizophrenia and were unsettled by ordinary sounds around that time. They have felt steady for about two years with regular outpatient follow-up.
profile.organization: Can describe a timeline clearly and distinguish minor variations from changes that matter to them.
profile.spontaneity: Engaged in conversation, volunteering personal details when they feel relevant.
profile.guardedness: Comfortable discussing health at the clinic, selective about sharing it with customers.
profile.expression: Generally relaxed and interested in talking about swimming and work.
profile.self_understanding: Feels able to recognize their usual responses to everyday stress and values having someone familiar to check in with.

facts.content: A noisy change machine at the laundry counter startled them last week. They found the stuck coin and went on with their shift.
facts.disclosure_context: An everyday incident they are comfortable discussing.

facts.content: They have not recently heard voices or felt that sounds had a personal message.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable reflecting on the change since earlier years.

facts.content: They usually swim before lunch on days off and feel pleasantly tired afterward.
facts.disclosure_context: An interest they like talking about.

facts.content: A longtime friend meets them for a drink after a swim a couple of times a month. They enjoy being able to discuss everyday stress.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable talking about this friendship.

facts.content: They take medication after brushing their teeth at night and want to discuss booking follow-up visits around rotating shifts.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss with the outpatient clinician.
